articles.headline: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic

When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.
